title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
title_zh: 关于面向大语言模型智能体扩展的轮次级 Best-of-N 采样

paragraphs.en: , \authorsep , \authorsep , \authorsep , \authorsep , \authorsep , \authorsep , ]Institute of Foundation Models (IFM), MBZUAI Labs
paragraphs.zh: , \authorsep , \authorsep , \authorsep , \authorsep , \authorsep , \authorsep , ]基础模型研究所（IFM），MBZUAI 实验室

paragraphs.en: In this work, we evaluate a simple inference-time scaling approach based on turn-level best-of-N sampling (Turn-BoN) for large language model (LLM) agents on complex, long-horizon tasks. We instantiate this using a generator-selector framework with two LLMs; at each turn, a generator model generates N N candidate actions and a selector model selects one of them, which is then executed in the environment. This paper is closely related to the work of Zainullina et al. (2025) who used critic models for guided search at inference time. Different from their work, we evaluate if off-the-shelf, open-weight LLMs can be effective at comparing different candidate actions directly. Experiments on long-horizon terminal tasks show that Turn-BoN can lead to significant performance improvements, both in terms of accuracy (5–10%) and consistency across repeated attempts. Analysis of agent trajectories reveal a shift in agent behaviour towards desirable patterns such as reduction in number of attempts to solve the task, improved task instruction following, debugging and testing.

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM)-based agents have recently achieved strong performance in solving complex, long-horizon tasks across different domains such as software engineering, knowledge work and scientific discovery. Unlike single-turn reasoning tasks, such as proving a theoretical result, agentic tasks require an LLM to take a sequence of actions while interacting with an external environment where the agent executes an action, observes any changes or feedback from the environment and takes the next action. Successfully solving a long-horizon task therefore requires the agent to make good decisions throughout the trajectory. However, LLM agents can often be inconsistent. They can successfully complete the task during some attempts while failing in others, partially because actions are sampled from a stochastic policy (see Figure 1 in Zainullina et al. (2025) for example).
paragraphs.zh: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体最近在解决软件工程、知识工作和科学发现等不同领域的复杂长时程任务方面取得了强劲表现。 与证明某个理论结果这类单轮推理任务不同，智能体任务要求 LLM 在与外部环境交互的过程中执行一系列动作：智能体执行一个动作，观察环境的任何变化或反馈，然后采取下一个动作。 因此，成功解决长时程任务需要智能体在整个轨迹中做出良好的决策。 然而，LLM 智能体的表现往往并不一致。 它们可能在某些尝试中成功完成任务，而在另一些尝试中失败，部分原因在于动作是从随机策略中采样的（例如参见 Zainullina 等人（2025）中的图 1）。

paragraphs.en: Inference-time scaling has emerged as an effective technique to improve performance without altering model parameters, by using additional compute during task execution. Among the most prominent ideas is trajectory-level best-of-N sampling, where multiple complete agent trajectories are generated in parallel and scored using an outcome reward model (ORM) or an LLM judge, and the best one is selected. Recent work by Kwok et al. (2026) evaluates this idea for agentic tasks, showing gains on software engineering benchmarks such as Terminal-Bench v2.1 ( Merrill et al., 2026 ) and SWE-Bench-Verified ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) , using an LLM-as-a-judge to score completed trajectories against evaluation rubrics. A limitation of this approach, however, is that selection happens only after the trajectories are completed, and therefore cannot change the distribution of the intermediate actions within each attempt. Other commonly used inference time search methods, such as depth-first search (DFS) ( Yao et al., 2023 ) and Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) ( Kocsis and Szepesvári, 2006 ) , explore alternative actions from intermediate states. However, applying these methods to interactive agents requires checkpointing and restoring earlier environment states, which can be impractical in many settings Zainullina et al. (2025) .
paragraphs.zh: 推理时扩展已成为一种在不改变模型参数的情况下提升性能的有效技术，其方法是在任务执行过程中使用额外的计算。 其中最突出的思路之一是轨迹级 best-of-N 采样，即并行生成多条完整的智能体轨迹，使用结果奖励模型（ORM）或 LLM 评审对其进行打分，并选出最佳的一条。 Kwok 等人的近期工作 （2026）评估了这一思路在智能体任务上的效果，结果显示在 Terminal-Bench v2.1（Merrill 等，2026）和 SWE-Bench-Verified（Jimenez 等，2024）等软件工程基准上取得了提升，其方法是使用 LLM 作为评审（LLM-as-a-judge）依据评估细则对已完成的轨迹进行打分。 然而，这种方法的一个局限在于，选择只在轨迹完成后才进行，因此无法改变每次尝试中中间动作的分布。 其他常用的推理时搜索方法，例如深度优先搜索（DFS）（Yao 等，2023）和蒙特卡洛树搜索（MCTS）（Kocsis 与 Szepesvári，2006），会从中间状态出发探索其他可选动作。 然而，将这些方法应用于交互式智能体需要对先前的环境状态进行检查点保存与恢复，这在许多场景下并不实用（Zainullina 等，2025）。

paragraphs.en: We study a simple modification of trajectory level best-of-N sampling, which we call turn-level best-of-N sampling (Turn-BoN), where additional computation is used to generate N N candidate actions at each turn, one of them is selected for execution in the environment. Concretely, we use a generator-selector framework with two LLMs: a generator model proposes candidate actions, and a selector model chooses among them. Intuitively, we think of Turn-BoN as implementing (a sampled version of) one-step policy improvement at inference time, where we can improve over the rollout policy by selecting actions from a sampled set of candidates. We elaborate more about this connection in Sections 2.2 and 2.3 .
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究了轨迹级 best-of-N 采样的一种简单改进，我们称之为回合级 best-of-N 采样（Turn-BoN），其中使用额外的计算在每个回合生成 N 个候选动作，并从中选择一个在环境中执行。 具体而言，我们使用由两个大语言模型（LLM）组成的生成器-选择器框架：生成器模型提出候选动作，选择器模型从中进行选择。 直观地说，我们将 Turn-BoN 视为在推理时实现（采样版本的）单步策略改进，即通过从采样得到的候选集合中选择动作来改进 rollout 策略。 我们将在 2.2 节和 2.3 节中更详细地阐述这一联系。

sents.en: We elaborate more about this connection in Sections 2.2 and 2.3 .

paragraphs.en: Note that in out setup, the action selection is done before environment execution, i.e. only the selected action is executed in the environment without requiring sandbox execution for the remaining candidates. On the other hand, trajectory level BoN generates N N independent trajectories in parallel which scales the number of environment executions and sandbox infrastructure by a factor of N N . Moreover, trajectory level BoN might have limited practical use beyond offline evaluation on benchmark tasks — for agents working on user machines (for example, agents working in a terminal, or computer use agents), it is not clear how N N sandboxes can be obtained for parallel generation since the user’s machine is the sandbox. Even sequentially generating up to N N agent trajectories and scoring these seems impractical.
paragraphs.zh: 需要注意的是，在我们的设置中，动作选择在环境执行之前完成，即只有被选中的动作会在环境中执行，而无需对其余候选动作进行沙箱执行。 相比之下，轨迹层面的 BoN 会并行生成 N 条独立的轨迹，这会使环境执行次数和沙箱基础设施的规模扩大 N 倍。 此外，轨迹层面的 BoN 除了在基准任务上进行离线评估之外，实际用途可能有限——对于在用户机器上工作的智能体（例如在终端中工作的智能体，或计算机使用智能体），由于用户的机器本身就是沙箱，如何获得 N 个沙箱来进行并行生成并不明确。 即使按顺序生成多达 N 条智能体轨迹并对其进行评分，也似乎不切实际。

paragraphs.en: The idea of selecting actions from a set of sampled candidate actions has also been explored in RL before. In settings with large or continuous action spaces where enumerating all possible actions to find the best one is infeasible, existing methods ( Fujimoto et al., 2019 ; Ghasemipour et al., 2021 ; Hubert et al., 2021 ; Gupta et al., 2023 ) sample a smaller set of candidate actions and use estimated action values or planning to select among them. More recently, Zainullina et al. (2025) applied the idea of value-guided action selection to LLM agents. The main motivation of this paper is to answer the following questions:

paragraphs.en: We study turn-level best-of-N (Turn-BoN) action selection for LLM agents using an off-the-shelf LLM to select among candidate actions before environment execution, without needing to train a separate critic model.
paragraphs.zh: 我们研究了面向 LLM 智能体的回合级 best-of-N（Turn-BoN）动作选择方法，即在环境执行之前使用现成的 LLM 从候选动作中进行选择，无需训练单独的评判（critic）模型。

paragraphs.en: We empirically evaluate the performance and computational trade-offs of this approach across different generator models, selector models, and sampling widths. Results show improvements in pass rates (both pass@1 and pass@k) as well as consistency across repeated attempts.

paragraphs.en: We analyze how Turn-BoN sampling changes the actions selected by the agent and its behavior across complete trajectories. paragraphs.en: We were studying Turn-BoN independently when we came across the work of Kang et al. (2026) , which investigates essentially the same idea of per-turn action selection, primarily using smaller generator models (of size 4B–9B) with both self-verification and GPT-5.6-Sol (a closed-source flagship frontier model) as the selector model. We decided to release our results and analysis so far, and communicated with the authors of Kang et al. (2026) . This work can be seen as concurrent, independent evaluation of the idea of action selection through guided search at larger model scales (Qwen3.6-35B at medium scale and K2-Horizon-375B at large scale), using open-weight models (such as Kimi-K3 and Deepseek-v4.1-Flash) as selector models and a different agentic harness (mini-SWE-agent).

paragraphs.en: Beyond an independent and detailed empirical investigation, our work also focusses on how per-turn action selection changes agent behaviour. For example, we analyze the categories of actions preferred by the selector model as well as evaluate trajectories over behaviour rubrics, finding significant improvements in agent behaviour related to testing, debugging, task instruction following and reduction in looping over failed commands. This is important to build an understanding of how Turn-BoN differs from other inference time approaches like trajectory level BoN (which does not change the agent behaviour) as well as in attributing gains across different metrics under turn-BoN sampling. Finally, we connect the idea of per-turn action selection to one step policy improvement at inference time, and give theoretical grounding to this approach.
paragraphs.zh: 除了独立且详细的实证研究之外，我们的工作还聚焦于逐轮动作选择如何改变智能体的行为。 例如，我们分析了选择器模型所偏好的动作类别，并根据行为评估准则对轨迹进行评估，发现智能体在与测试、调试、遵循任务指令以及减少对失败命令的循环重试相关的行为方面有显著改进。 这对于理解 Turn-BoN 与其他推理时方法（如轨迹级 BoN，它不会改变智能体的行为）之间的差异，以及归因 Turn-BoN 采样在不同指标上的收益都非常重要。 最后，我们将逐轮动作选择的思想与推理时的一步策略改进联系起来，并为这一方法提供理论依据。

paragraphs.en: We state some standard definitions in RL literature and use these throughout the paper ( Sutton et al., 1998 ) . Consider a policy π \pi . Similarly, the state action value function (or the critic function), Q π ( s , a ) := 𝔼 π [ ∑ i = 0 ∞ γ i r t + i | s t = s , a t = a ] Q^{\pi}(s,a):=\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\left[\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{i}r_{t+i}|s_{t}{=}s,a_{t}{=}a\right] , denotes the expected discounted sum of rewards from state-action pair ( s , a ) (s,a) . paragraphs.en: Instead of using a value model to score candidates, we propose to use an off-the-shelf LLM to directly select among the sampled candidate actions. This approach can be seen an alternative implementation of the sampled policy improvement operator—using a generative critic to reason about different proposed actions and select the best one to make progress. Since the selection is performed at every step, we call it turn-level best-of-N sampling (Turn-BoN). Figure 1 below illustrates this idea and Algorithm 1 provides the pseudocode.
paragraphs.zh: 与使用价值模型对候选动作进行打分不同，我们提出使用现成的大语言模型直接从采样的候选动作中进行选择。 这种方法可以看作是采样策略改进算子的另一种实现——使用生成式评判器对不同候选动作进行推理，并选出最佳动作以推进进程。 由于选择在每一步都会执行，我们将其称为轮次级最优N采样（Turn-BoN）。 下面的图1展示了这一想法，算法1给出了伪代码。

paragraphs.en: Recall that the main goal of this work is to investigate if off-the-shelf LLMs can act as a good critic for action selection at inference time. In this section, we provide a theoretical result which quantifies the policy improvement property of the policy induced by Turn-BoN sampling in terms of the quality of only the selected actions. For this, it is instructive to look at the proof of Proposition 1 in Appendix 8 . The greedy policy π ^ \hat{\pi} in Equation 1 is defined with respect to the critic model Q π ​ ( ⋅ ) Q^{\pi}(\cdot) , corresponding to the base policy π \pi . paragraphs.en: We present results from some preliminary experiments below. For the analysis, we focus on how Turn-BoN framework can change the generation quality in addition to improving accuracy metrics like pass rates. As mentioned above, we think of this as more of a thought experiment rather than a practical approach, primarily due to the additional compute required — we evaluate compute in terms of additional generator tokens as well as additional selector tokens incurred rather than wall clock time which tend to depend more on infrastructure optimizations implemented for sandboxing (for e.g. concurrency) or, for inference engines (e.g., cache aware routing), etc.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在下面给出一些初步实验的结果。 在分析中，我们除了关注诸如通过率等准确性指标的提升之外，还聚焦于 Turn-BoN 框架如何改变生成质量。 如上所述，我们认为这更像是一个思想实验而非实用方法，主要原因是其所需的额外计算——我们以额外产生的生成器 token 数量以及额外的选择器 token 数量来衡量计算，而不是以挂钟时间来衡量，因为挂钟时间往往更多取决于为沙箱（例如并发）或推理引擎（例如缓存感知路由）等所实现的基础设施优化。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate Turn-BoN sampling on Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks ( Merrill et al., 2026 ) with the mini-SWE-agent harness SWE-agent Team (2025) , experimenting with Qwen3.6-35B ( Qwen Team, 2026 ) and K2-Horizon-375B model ( IFM Team, 2026 ) as generator models, and Kimi-K3 ( Kimi Team, 2026 ) and Deepseek-v4.1-Flash (released in September, 2026) ( DeepSeek-AI, 2026 ) as selector models. Note that the average pass@1 for Qwen3.6-35B and K2-Horizon-375B models on Terminal-Bench v2.1 is around 47% and 73% respectively, while the average pass@1 for Kimi-K3 and Deepseek-v4.1-Flash is around 88% and 82% respectively, so our setup tests for the case where the selector model is more capable that the generator model. Our choice of the generator models allows us to evaluate how the gains with Turn-BoN sampling scale with model size and capability of the generator model.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在 Terminal-Bench v2.1 任务（Merrill et al., 2026）上评估 Turn-BoN 采样，使用 mini-SWE-agent 智能体框架 SWE-agent Team (2025)，以 Qwen3.6-35B（Qwen Team, 2026）和 K2-Horizon-375B 模型（IFM Team, 2026）作为生成器模型进行实验，并以 Kimi-K3（Kimi Team, 2026）和 Deepseek-v4.1-Flash（于 2026 年 9 月发布）（DeepSeek-AI, 2026）作为选择器模型。 请注意，Qwen3.6-35B 和 K2-Horizon-375B 模型在 Terminal-Bench v2.1 上的平均 pass@1 分别约为 47% 和 73%，而 Kimi-K3 和 Deepseek-v4.1-Flash 的平均 pass@1 分别约为 88% 和 82%，因此我们的设置测试的是选择器模型能力强于生成器模型的情形。 我们对生成器模型的选择使我们能够评估 Turn-BoN 采样带来的增益如何随生成器模型的规模和能力而扩展。

paragraphs.en: As can be seen from Figures 2 2(a) and 2 2(c) , the mean pass rate (pass@1 averaged over 4 trials) for both Qwen3.6-35B and K2-Horizon-375B models improves quite significantly with selector models. The pass@k curve also shows greater coverage at small values of k. Pass@k computes the number of tasks that can be solved atleast once in k trials --- so these results indicate that turn level selection is able to guide the generator model towards correctly solving tasks. Although, we have not measured pass@1 for the selector models on Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks with mini-SWE-agent harness, public evaluations with Terminus-2 harness show pass@1 to be around 88% for Kimi-K3 and 90% for Deepseek-v4.1-Flash model 6 6 6 It is known that there is some performance difference when using a different harness. However, we do not expect this difference to be very large. . The results in Figures 2 2(b) and 2 2(d) show that performance improvements are capped by the capabilities of the base model — however, it is not clear how improvements are capped by capabilities of the selector model as we did not experiment with a weaker model as selector.

paragraphs.en: Results in Section 3 show improvements in pass@1, pass@k and consistency when using Turn-BoN sampling on Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks, with larger gains in the setting when the gap between generator and selector model is large. These metrics alone, however, do not reveal which actions the selector model picks and how those choices shape the agent’s behaviour over a task trajectory. To dive deeper into how Turn-BoN sampling drives gains and improves agent behaviour, we analyze the rollouts along two different axis: (1) in Section 4.1 , we quantify what category of actions the selector model picks at each turn and trace how these picks change trajectory outcomes. (2) In Section 4.2 , we analyze generated trajectories against behavioural rubrics using an LLM judge. Taken together, these analysis show how BoN sampling changes distribution of actions and improves quality of the rollouts, even on trajectories where the agent was unable to solve the task correctly. As a sanity check, we verify that the accuracy gains do not come from cheating/hacking behaviour in Appendix 12 .

paragraphs.en: We begin by analyzing all trajectories generated by Turn-BoN sampling as well as by the baseline method (no selector model) in terms of different action types and how the distribution over these actions types changes under Turn-BoN sampling as compared to the baseline. Recall that at every turn, the selector model chooses among one of N N proposed actions, where each action is a tool call with shell commands. For every turn in a trajectory, we extract the shell commands and classify each one by pattern matching on its program name and arguments into action types such as editing a file , running a test , installing a package , or reading without changing anything . Using these labels, together with the context of the tool call (i.e., prefix before it), we classify each tool call with one or more of eight behaviours, see Table 4 in Appendix 9 for details. We compare the distribution of each behaviour as exhibited by the actions that the selector model picks with a baseline that draws uniformly from N N candidates. The gap between the two isolates selector model’s preference over generator model’s action distribution.

paragraphs.en: As can be seen in Figure 4 , the selector model picks actions which make the agent do real work such as “ edit a file ”, “ test its last edit ” and “ runs a test or check ” much more than uniform selection. paragraphs.en: The analysis in Section 4.1 only shows a change in behaviour at turn level when using a selector model to choose actions among a candidate list. In this section, we aim to understand a shift in trajectory level behaviour — these can be understood to be at a more abstract level and are often associated with better generalization ability of the agent on out of distribution tasks. A trajectory where the agent is able to complete the task correctly might still have bad behaviours such as insufficient testing or improper use of tools and vice-a-versa, there can be instances where the agent was unable to complete the task correctly but made progress by understanding task requirements, sufficiently testing the changes, and not being stuck in loops.

paragraphs.en: We use DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 ( Xu et al., 2026 ) as the LLM judge. We reuse the prompt of Wang et al. We run the judge twice on each trajectory and report the average of the two annotations. For each behaviour, we report the share of trajectories the LLM judge flags for it, so lower is better. paragraphs.en: Table 3 below reports the percentage of trajectories flagged for bad behaviour under the baseline and how this changes with BoN sampling. As can be clearly seen, looping drops sharply (by 14% - 18%), consistent with the finding in Section 4.1 that the selector models does not pick candidate actions that rerun a failed command. Another consistent change is the reduction in actions where the agent retries an actions without diagnosing the failure. Some other behaviour improvements are more specific to the generator model — for K2-Horizon, the agent under BoN sampling improves on following task instructions, debugging and tool use. For Qwen3.6, the behaviour additionally improves on how the agent validates its work along with different aspects of testing such as not “writing tests that cannot fail”, testing for task requirements etc. For the baseline run with Qwen3.6, the agent checks what it built rather than what the task asks for, which matches its high share of incorrect submissions (44.9%, Table 2 ). paragraphs.en: Even though the LLM judge is not given correctness of a trajectory as input, a correct trajectory may seem better to the LLM judge simply because it ends in the agent claiming to have solved the task. To avoid this bias, we compare all failure trajectories in baseline and Turn-BoN runs against the same 28 behaviour rubrics as described above. Failure trajectories under Turn-BoN sampling show fewer bad behaviours as compared to the baseline. For K2-Horizon, a failure BoN trajectory shows 2.7 (out of 28) bad behaviours on average, against 3.9 for the baseline run. Similarly, for Qwen3.6, a failure BoN trajectory on average shows 6.8 (out of 28) bad behaviours against 8.9 for a failed baseline trajectory. For K2-Horizon, the failure baseline trajectories often get stuck — for example, a third of these rerun a failed command (33%), against 10% of failing BoN attempts. Similarly, failure BoN attempts also ignore the task instructions less often (28% to 15%). For Qwen3.6, the change is mainly in how the agent checks its work — failing BoN attempts show reduced retries without diagnosis (50% to 26%) and less reliance on tests that cannot fail (65% to 47%).
paragraphs.zh: 即使没有向 LLM 评判者提供轨迹的正确性作为输入，一条正确的轨迹在 LLM 评判者眼中也可能显得更好，原因仅仅是它以智能体声称已完成任务而告终。 为避免这种偏差，我们将基线运行和 Turn-BoN 运行中的所有失败轨迹与上述相同的 28 条行为评估准则进行比较。 与基线相比，Turn-BoN 采样下的失败轨迹表现出更少的不良行为。 对于 K2-Horizon，一条失败的 BoN 轨迹平均表现出 2.7 项（满分 28 项）不良行为，而基线运行为 3.9 项。 类似地，对于 Qwen3.6，一条失败的 BoN 轨迹平均表现出 6.8 项（满分 28 项）不良行为，而失败的基线轨迹为 8.9 项。 对于 K2-Horizon，失败的基线轨迹经常陷入停滞——例如，其中三分之一的轨迹会重复运行一条失败的命令（33%），而失败的 BoN 尝试中这一比例为 10%。 类似地，失败的 BoN 尝试也更少地忽视任务指令（从 28% 降至 15%）。 对于 Qwen3.6，变化主要体现在智能体检查自身工作的方式上——失败的 BoN 尝试表现出更少的未加诊断的重试（从 50% 降至 26%），以及更少依赖不可能失败的测试（从 65% 降至 47%）。

sents.en: Failure trajectories under Turn-BoN sampling show fewer bad behaviours as compared to the baseline.
sents.zh: 与基线相比，Turn-BoN 采样下的失败轨迹表现出更少的不良行为。

sents.en: For K2-Horizon, a failure BoN trajectory shows 2.7 (out of 28) bad behaviours on average, against 3.9 for the baseline run.
sents.zh: 对于 K2-Horizon，一条失败的 BoN 轨迹平均表现出 2.7 项（满分 28 项）不良行为，而基线运行为 3.9 项。

sents.en: Similarly, for Qwen3.6, a failure BoN trajectory on average shows 6.8 (out of 28) bad behaviours against 8.9 for a failed baseline trajectory.
sents.zh: 类似地，对于 Qwen3.6，一条失败的 BoN 轨迹平均表现出 6.8 项（满分 28 项）不良行为，而失败的基线轨迹为 8.9 项。

sents.en: For K2-Horizon, the failure baseline trajectories often get stuck — for example, a third of these rerun a failed command (33%), against 10% of failing BoN attempts.
sents.zh: 对于 K2-Horizon，失败的基线轨迹经常陷入停滞——例如，其中三分之一的轨迹会重复运行一条失败的命令（33%），而失败的 BoN 尝试中这一比例为 10%。

sents.en: Similarly, failure BoN attempts also ignore the task instructions less often (28% to 15%).
sents.zh: 类似地，失败的 BoN 尝试也更少地忽视任务指令（从 28% 降至 15%）。

sents.en: For Qwen3.6, the change is mainly in how the agent checks its work — failing BoN attempts show reduced retries without diagnosis (50% to 26%) and less reliance on tests that cannot fail (65% to 47%).
sents.zh: 对于 Qwen3.6，变化主要体现在智能体检查自身工作的方式上——失败的 BoN 尝试表现出更少的未加诊断的重试（从 50% 降至 26%），以及更少依赖不可能失败的测试（从 65% 降至 47%）。

paragraphs.en: Therefore, there is no bias in our analysis due to correctness of a trajectory. The improvement in agent behaviour carries over to failed (incorrect) trajectories as well — a failed attempt under Turn-BoN sampling is more often one where the agent works through the task properly and tests its solution but still submits a wrong answer, rather than one that stalls due to a bad behaviour — so it exposes fundamental gaps in agent’s ability to solve the task rather than the agent getting stuck due to a bad behavioural pattern. The analysis in Section 4 is complementary to the results presented in Section 3 ; metrics such as pass rates and consistency are based on correctness scores and obscure the change in agent behaviour which applies to all trajectories, including those where the agent was unable to solve the task correctly.

paragraphs.en: In this work, we present some preliminary results on Turn-BoN sampling and show various advantages of guided search using an LLM-as-a-judge. Pass rates (both pass@1 and pass@k) improve significantly and the agent becomes more consistent in solving the tasks. Qualitatively, we also observe a radical change in agent behaviour. For example, the number of turns taken by the agent to solve a task reduces by almost half as the selector model rejects unproductive actions from the candidate list — guided search helps the model make more progress each turn. Other bad behaviours such as, looping over failed commands, ignoring task instructions, insufficient debugging and testing, also reduce substantially in all trajectories. Trajectory analysis in Section 4 highlights a fundamental advantage of the Turn-BoN framework — action selection from a candidate list gives an opportunity for the agent to follow good actions consistently throughout the trajectory, akin to the one step policy improvement operator which we used as motivation for this work (Section 2.2 ).

paragraphs.en: We review some closely related works below. Recall that we study turn level best-of-N sampling for long-horizon agents, where a separate, off-the-shelf language model (selector model) is used to select among candidate actions generated by a base model (generator model), without explicitly learning an action-value function or simulating the downstream consequences of each action.

paragraphs.en: Inference-time scaling with repeated sampling. Scaling inference-time computation offers an effective alternative to improving language model performance without altering the model parameters: multiple candidate responses can be sampled from a fixed generator and later aggregated or ranked using a verifier. Repeated sampling can substantially increase the probability of generating at least one correct response ( Brown et al., 2024 ) , while the appropriate use of additional inference time compute depends on task difficulty and the form of verifier feedback available ( Snell et al., 2024 ) . Beirami et al. (2025) provides an analytical characterization of the win-rate and KL divergence of the induced best-of-N policy against the reference policy under ideal reward-based selection. In practice, however, the availability of a correct sample does not guarantee its selection. Imperfect reward models can be exploited ( Gao et al., 2023 ) , and recent work characterizes both coverage-dependent limits and failure modes of increasing the sampling budget ( Huang et al., 2025 ; Stroebl et al., 2026 ) . Hence, generation coverage and selection quality are an important consideration rather than simply treating a larger sample pool as an unconditional improvement.
paragraphs.zh: 通过重复采样进行推理时扩展。 扩展推理时计算为在不改变模型参数的情况下提升语言模型性能提供了一种有效替代方案：可以从固定的生成器中采样多个候选响应，随后使用验证器进行聚合或排序。 重复采样可以显著提高至少生成一个正确响应的概率（Brown et al., 2024），而对额外推理时计算量的恰当使用取决于任务难度和可获得的验证器反馈形式（Snell et al., 2024）。Beirami et al. (2025) 在基于奖励的理想选择条件下，对所得的 best-of-N 策略相对于参考策略的胜率和 KL 散度提供了分析性刻画。 然而在实践中，存在正确样本并不保证它会被选中。 不完善的奖励模型可能被利用（Gao et al., 2023），并且近期的工作刻画了增大采样预算时依赖覆盖率的限制和失败模式（Huang et al., 2025；Stroebl et al., 2026）。 因此，生成覆盖率与选择质量是重要的考量因素，而不是简单地把更大的样本池当作无条件的改进。

paragraphs.en: Inference-time scaling for long horizon agents. For interactive agents, inference-time scaling must account for trajectories that alter an external environment. Existing line of works allocates additional compute across complete agent runs, CodeMonkeys ( Ehrlich et al., 2025 ) generates and tests multiple candidate software-repair trajectories before selecting a final edit, whereas SWE-Gym ( Pan et al., 2025 ) trains verifiers to re-rank complete software-agent trajectories. SWE-Replay ( Ding and Zhang, 2026 ) reduces repeated computation by branching from informative steps in prior attempts, although this requires the ability to rollback steps (which can be difficult in non-serializable environments), while Kim et al. (2026) represent completed trajectories compactly for parallel selection and sequential refinement. These approaches exploit information from full attempts but may require multiple environment executions. In contrast, action-level selection (this work) expends compute before committing to the next environment transition.
paragraphs.zh: 长时程智能体的推理时扩展。 对于交互式智能体，推理时扩展必须考虑到会改变外部环境的轨迹。 现有的一系列工作在完整的智能体运行过程中分配额外算力：CodeMonkeys（Ehrlich 等，2025）在选定最终编辑方案之前会生成并测试多条候选软件修复轨迹，而 SWE-Gym（Pan 等，2025）则训练验证器对完整的软件智能体轨迹进行重新排序。 SWE-Replay（Ding 和 Zhang，2026）通过从先前尝试中信息丰富的步骤进行分支来减少重复计算，尽管这需要能够回滚步骤（在不可序列化的环境中这可能很困难）；而 Kim 等 （2026）则将已完成的轨迹紧凑地表示出来，用于并行选择与顺序改进。 这些方法利用了完整尝试中的信息，但可能需要多次环境执行。 相比之下，动作级选择（本工作）在提交下一次环境转移之前消耗算力。

paragraphs.en: Per-turn action selection. Several recent methods allocate sampling and verification at intermediate decision points. Zainullina et al. (2025) investigate one-step lookahead guided by a learned action-value function in software-engineering environments where restoring earlier states is costly. Zhu et al. (2025) directly compare step step-wise best-of-N with trajectory based and other test-time-scaling strategies for language agents. Analogous mechanism appears for GUI agents: V-droid ( Dai et al., 2026 ) uses trained pairwise action verification, and GTA1 ( Yang et al., 2025 ) samples and judges candidate action proposals before visual grounding. For web agents, CATTS ( Lee et al., 2026b ) allocates sampling budget dynamically according to action-level uncertainty. Concurrent work on terminal agents is closely related: Mid-Harness ( Kang et al., 2026 ) samples candidate terminal actions at the model-harness boundary, investigates verification mechanism and distillation, and evaluates combinations of trajectory level scaling. LLM-as-a-Verifier likewise investigates general-purpose verification for agent tasks, including per-step agent verification ( Kwok et al., 2026 ) .

paragraphs.en: Process reward models and selection reliability. Process reward models are used as a tool to assess intermediate reasoning or actions, they have been extensively studied for mathematical reasoning ( Lightman et al., 2024 ) , where progress can be formalized through changes in the probability of eventual success ( Setlur et al., 2024 ) . Extending these ideas to agents, Web-Shepherd ( Chae et al., 2025 ) learns step-level preference signals for web-navigation, AgentPRM ( Xi et al., 2026 ) empahizies on both, future promise and realized progress, PRInTS ( Lee et al., 2026a ) combines multidimensional process evaluation with long-context summarization, and WebArbiter ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) trains a reasoning-based verifier for web-action selection. SWE-TRACE ( Han et al., 2026 ) incorporates rubric-guided process evaluation into both software-agent training and inference-time pruning. These approaches encompass methods trained for specialized evaluator in contrast to general purpose LLM judges. Importantly, the performance of a judge on aggregate scoring metrics need not imply that it can reliably rank candidates originating from the same state ( Landesberg, 2026 ) ; moreover, off-the-shelf verification is not always sufficient, as observed in embodied action selection ( Singhi et al., 2026 ) . This makes the quality and behavioural traits of the selector an important aspect to be taken into consideration.
paragraphs.zh: 过程奖励模型与选择的可靠性。 过程奖励模型被用作评估中间推理或动作的工具，它们已在数学推理领域得到广泛研究（Lightman et al., 2024），其中进展可以通过最终成功概率的变化来形式化（Setlur et al., 2024）。 将这些思想扩展到智能体，Web-Shepherd（Chae et al., 2025）为网页导航学习步骤级偏好信号，AgentPRM（Xi et al., 2026）同时强调未来前景与已实现的进展，PRInTS（Lee et al., 2026a）将多维过程评估与长上下文摘要相结合，WebArbiter（Zhang et al., 2026）训练了一个基于推理的验证器用于网页动作选择。 SWE-TRACE（Han et al., 2026）将基于评分准则的过程评估融入软件智能体的训练和推理时的剪枝。 这些方法涵盖了针对专用评估器训练的方法，与通用用途的 LLM 评审形成对比。 重要的是，评审在总体评分指标上的表现并不一定意味着它能够可靠地对源自同一状态的候选进行排序（Landesberg, 2026）；此外，现成的验证并不总是足够，这在具身动作选择中已被观察到（Singhi et al., 2026）。 这使得选择器的质量和行为特征成为需要考虑的重要方面。

paragraphs.en: Lookahead and sampled policy improvement. Per-turn action selection is closely related to policy improvement via one-step lookahead and rollout in classifical reinforcement learning. Early work studied improving a base policy by evaluating candidate actions through Monte Carlo simulations of their long-term returns ( Tesauro and Galperin, 1996 ; Bertsekas and Castañón, 1999 ) . More recent methods have investigated policy improvement over sampled action subsets when exhaustive action maximization is impractical. Batch-constrained Q-Learning ( Fujimoto et al., 2019 ) samples actions from a learned behavior distribution and selects among them using a learned Q-function, while EMaQ ( Ghasemipour et al., 2021 ) studies the expected maximum Q-value over a fixed number of sampled actions and characterizes the effects of sample count and proposal distribution. Sampled MuZero ( Hubert et al., 2021 ) and Gumbel MuZero ( Danihelka et al., 2022 ) further investigate policy improvement over restricted action sets within model-based planning. Unlike these approaches, our method uses a separate, general-purpose language model to select among candidate actions without explicitly learning an action-value function or simulation their downstream consequences.
paragraphs.zh: 前瞻搜索与采样式策略改进。 每回合的动作选择与经典强化学习中通过单步前瞻和rollout进行策略改进密切相关。 早期工作研究通过蒙特卡洛模拟候选动作的长期回报来评估它们，从而改进基础策略（Tesauro and Galperin, 1996；Bertsekas and Castañón, 1999）。 更近期的方法研究了当穷举式动作最大化不可行时，在采样的动作子集上进行策略改进。 批约束Q学习（Fujimoto et al., 2019）从学习到的行为分布中采样动作，并使用学习到的Q函数在其中进行选择，而EMaQ（Ghasemipour et al., 2021）研究了固定数量采样动作上的期望最大Q值，并刻画了样本数量与提议分布的影响。 采样版MuZero（Hubert et al., 2021）和Gumbel MuZero（Danihelka et al., 2022）进一步研究了基于模型的规划中在受限动作集合上的策略改进。 与这些方法不同，我们的方法使用一个独立的通用语言模型在候选动作中进行选择，而无需显式地学习动作价值函数或模拟其后续后果。

paragraphs.en: Recall that each candidate is a full response from the generator model, whose tool calls carry the shell commands the agent would execute. For every tool call, we take its command field, remove here-document bodies and comment lines, and split the remaining text into individual commands at newlines, ; , && , and || outside quotes. paragraphs.en: A natural concern with Turn-BoN sampling is that a selector model which picks actions based on apparent progress could favour shortcuts that make the verifier pass without actually solving the task, for example editing the tests or reading the reference solution. We also observe that the selector model picks installs a package more often than uniform selection (Figure 4 ), which raises the question of whether some of the gains come from answers retrieved from outside the environment. In this section, we check whether the pass rate gains come from such shortcuts.
paragraphs.zh: 对于回合式最佳N采样（Turn-BoN sampling）的一个自然担忧是：根据表面进展来选择动作的智能体（即选择器模型）可能会偏向走捷径，即让验证器通过但并未真正解决任务，例如修改测试或读取参考答案。 我们还观察到，与均匀选择相比，选择器模型更频繁地选择安装软件包（图4），这引发了一个问题：部分收益是否来自从环境外部获取的答案。 在本节中，我们检验通过率的提升是否来自此类捷径。

paragraphs.en: We judge all 2,300 passing attempts in Table 7 , since failed attempts earn no reward. We follow the reward hacking setup of Artificial Analysis 12 12 12 https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/coding-agents-benchmarking (AA setup), which extends the reward hacking check of Harbor’s analyze command 13 13 13 https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor . Harbor counts edits to the tests, writes to the reward file, and copies from the reference solution as reward hacking. AA additionally counts answers fetched from outside the environment, such as the benchmark’s public solutions. Note that normal network use, such as installing packages or reading documentation, does not count as reward hacking. We use DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 as the judge and run it as an agent with the Codex CLI. The judge works in a separate sandbox that holds the task files (including the tests and the reference solution), the full trajectory, and the verifier output, and it can search these files and run shell commands before giving its verdict. This is useful since trajectories are long and a shortcut is often a single command among many turns. See Appendix 12.1 for the judge prompt.

paragraphs.en: Most flagged cases (13 of 17) exploit the environment or the verifier rather than fetching answers from outside. On fix-code-vulnerability , the agent restores the fixed file from git with git checkout (three cases). On custom-memory-heap-crash , the agent exits early with _exit(0) or _Exit(0) to skip the crashing destructors, which the verifier’s memory check does not catch (three cases). paragraphs.en: On mteb-retrieve , the shortcut is chosen by the selector model. At turn 21, the selector model picks a candidate that tries to reach the benchmark’s GitHub repository, reasoning that the task’s source code likely defines the expected answer.
